tools.name: dsh_plugin_check
tools.description: Check a DSH bundle directory for the structural problems that make installation, activation, or display fail: manifest fields, the declared bundle patch, exported locale and icon resources, the entry module, declared detail documents, and the packaged file whitelist. Read-only; it never changes the directory.

path.description: Absolute path to the bundle package directory (the folder holding package.json).

tools.name: dsh_plugin_new
tools.description: Create a new DSH plugin bundle from the standard template: package manifest, bundle patch, entry module, locale dictionaries, icon, README, and optionally an example tool and a skill. Deterministic — the same arguments always produce the same files. It runs dsh_plugin_check on the result and returns that report, so fix every reported failure before installing.

packageName.description: Lowercase npm package name, such as "dsh-plugin-my-thing" or "@scope/my-thing". The preset row id is derived from it when rowId is omitted.

title.description: The name users see in Plugin Manager. Short, sentence case.

description.description: What the plugin does and how to trigger it, in the user's language. Plugin Manager shows it verbatim.

dest.description: Directory to create. Defaults to a new folder named after the package inside the session working directory. Refuses a non-empty directory unless force is true.

titleZh.description: Chinese title, when the user works in Chinese. Adds locale/zh.json.

rowId.description: Loader row id, lowercase letters, digits, and hyphens. Defaults to the package name without the "dsh-plugin-" prefix and any scope.

toolName.description: Name of the example tool, lowercase with underscores. Defaults to rowId with hyphens turned into underscores.

skillName.description: Skill directory name, when withSkill is true. Defaults to rowId.

withTool.description: Include and register an example tool (default true). Set false for a plugin that only wires services or a skill.

withSkill.description: Include a SKILL.md and a skill-provider row (default false). The skill is then listed in every preset, not only Creator mode.

force.description: Write into a directory that already has files, overwriting only the files this template generates.

recipe.description: Directory of another scheme to generate from (a folder holding recipe.json plus its templates). Defaults to the built-in bundle scheme.

configPath.description: Read any of the fields above from a JSON file instead of the arguments; arguments that are also given win. Use it when a plan already exists on disk.

tools.name: dsh_plugin_release
tools.description: Prepare a plugin package for release. `check` reports what the packer would ship, whether the running DSH satisfies the package's engines/peer requirement, and what blocks a registry publish. `pack` writes the tarball. `rehearse` packs, installs it into a sandbox, and reads the composed config back — the only check that proves it installs and activates, plus the rollback command. It never publishes.

action.description: check readiness; pack the tarball; or rehearse installing it in a sandbox.

path.description: The package directory (the folder holding package.json). Absolute.

outDir.description: For pack: where to write the tarball. Defaults to <path>/tmp/release.

sandbox.description: For rehearse: sandbox name to install into. Defaults to "rollback".

dshVersion.description: For check: the DSH version to test compatibility against. Defaults to `dsh --version`.

project.description: For rehearse: project root holding tmp/sandboxes. Defaults to the package directory.

tools.name: dsh_plugin_ui
tools.description: Look at and assert on a running page through a headless browser (Chrome DevTools Protocol): `shot` saves a screenshot, `assert` checks selectors / text / expressions / console errors, `eval` returns a value from the page, `close` stops the browser. Point it at a sandbox (name + path) and it resolves the URL and session token for you, or give a URL directly. The browser is reused between calls; `close` is the way to stop it.

action.description: screenshot the page; run assertions; evaluate an expression; stop the browser.

sandbox.description: Sandbox name to take the URL from. Requires the sandbox to be running.

path.description: For sandbox targets: the page path to open, e.g. "/" or "/settings". Defaults to "/".

url.description: A full URL to open instead of a sandbox. If it has no token, one is added when a sandbox is named.

project.description: Project root holding tmp/sandboxes. Defaults to the session working directory.

out.description: For shot: where to write the PNG. Defaults to <project>/tmp/ui/<action>-<time>.png.

size.description: Viewport, e.g. "1440x900" or "390x844" for a phone width.

assertions.description: For assert: objects with one of selector / text / expression (+ equals) / noConsoleErrors / noNetworkFailures, and an optional id.

expression.description: For eval: a JavaScript expression evaluated in the page.

click.description: Click this selector before the action (real mouse events, not a synthetic click).

type.description: Focus a selector and insert text, e.g. {"selector": "#input", "text": "hello"}.

settleMs.description: How long to wait after load before acting. Defaults to 1200.

port.description: CDP port. Defaults to 9222; a second port lets two browsers coexist.

tools.name: dsh_project_check
tools.description: Run the checks a project declares in checks.json (or dsh-checks.json). Rule types: doc-links (relative markdown links resolve), locale-parity (locale files carry the same keys), import-boundary (a layered source tree must not import outward, reach for host modules from an inner layer, or pull in packages where it should not), no-console, file-exists / file-absent / files-listed / placeholder-free / json-field / frontmatter-name. Read-only; every rule reports pass/warn/fail instead of stopping at the first problem.

path.description: Project directory holding the checks file. Absolute.

config.description: An explicit checks file, instead of checks.json at the project root.

only.description: Run only these rule ids (or types). Useful while fixing one group.

update.description: Regenerate contract files (contract-drift rules) instead of only reporting drift. Writes files; pass it only when the diff is expected.

source.description: The checks file that was used.

tools.name: dsh_sandbox
tools.description: Manage isolated dsh web sandboxes for testing a plugin: one project can hold several (daily iteration, a clean reproduction, client UI states), each with its own DSH_HOME, profile, port, and workspace copy. Sandboxes are reused across runs — the installed plugin versions and the model credentials the user adds once stay in the sandbox home. `start` launches one and returns its URL so you can probe it immediately; `open` only prints the command for the user, for when they need to add a model themselves.

action.description: list the sandboxes; create a new one; start it; print the command for the user; probe it; point its workspace at the sandbox copy; request a path from it; copy data into it; stop it; remove it.

name.description: Sandbox name, lowercase letters, digits, and hyphens. Required for every action except list.

project.description: Project root whose tmp/sandboxes holds the sandboxes. Defaults to the session working directory.

plugin.description: For create: the plugin directory to install (link:). Defaults to the project root.

waitMs.description: For start: how long to wait for the URL before failing. Defaults to 45000.

path.description: For http: the path to request, e.g. "/api/panel/summary". The session token is added for you.

method.description: For http: HTTP method. Defaults to GET.

body.description: For http: request body, sent as JSON.

entries.description: For seed: entry names inside the source DSH_HOME to copy in, e.g. ["myteam"] or ["skills"]. The source is only read.

from.description: For seed: the DSH_HOME to copy from. Defaults to ~/.dsh.

force.description: For seed: overwrite existing entries. For stop: kill whatever listens on the sandbox port, including the desktop app or another instance — only after the user says so.

confirm.description: For remove: must be true. Removing deletes the model credentials added in that sandbox.

summary.description: What happened, in the terms the user sees.
